chapter_theme: The last seven verses to the heart: it has taken the lead in the mind's realm beyond speech, joined the awareness that fills every land and time, come to a life that is not living, drunk the toddy of bliss that does not cloy, and, with habit, fixed contemplation and even the kingdom of silence left behind, gained the place without difference. The work ends by crediting the whole attainment to the holy feet of the guru, which swept the heart's bondage away as the sun takes the dew.
structure_note: 801 to 805 continue the states and negations of the first run; 806 and 807 are two closing similes, mercury rejoining mercury and the sun on the dew, and 807 alone names the guru.

801.reading: In the mind's realm that stands past speech, heart, you took the lead in that which stands without a blow.
801.nuance: மனோகோசரம் is what lies within the mind's range, so the verse places the attainment beyond words but not beyond mind, where the common formula (வாக்கு மனாதீதம்) puts it beyond both; the compound may instead mean the mind's own realm as the field in which speech has ceased. தாக்கறவே, without a strike or impact, is agitation ended. தலைசெய்தாய் is to excel or to become the head, and the sense is approximate.

802.reading: Filling every land and excelling in every time, heart, you joined the place of the awareness that is awareness itself.
802.nuance: சித்தாய சித்து is chit that is chit, pure awareness as its own nature, in the Vedantic sense of sat-chit-ananda; சித்து is also the Siddhars' word for attainment and the siddha, and the phrase can be heard as 'the attained attainment'. The verse gives the heart the Supreme's two marks, pervading space and time.

803.reading: Neither sinking nor stretching, filled as that very nature, heart, you came to live a life that is not living.
803.nuance: தன்மயம், of its own nature or absorbed into it, makes the heart the substance rather than a thing in it. வாழாதே வாழ, to live without living, matches 786's sleeping without sleeping: the life of the person has stopped and a life goes on that is not his.

804.reading: Drinking within and without the toddy of bliss that never cloys, heart, you set your eye on that which stands.
804.nuance: கள், toddy, is the figure for an intoxication that does not stale (உவட்டாத); the Puranamalai's honey that does not cloy (773) is the same claim. உள்ளும் புறம்பும், within and without, is where the drinking happens, so the bliss is not inner only.

805.reading: With habit gone, fixed contemplation gone, even the great kingdom of silence gone, heart, you gained the place that stands without difference.
805.nuance: வாதனை is vasana, the residue of past action and habit; நிஷ்டை is nishta, the fixed absorption of practice; மா மௌன ராச்சியம், the great kingdom of silence, is the sage's silence itself. All three are passed, so the state of the silent sage, which the Siddhars usually make the goal, is here a stage left behind; what remains is defined only as பேதமற, without difference.

806.reading: As mercury that has been parted mingles again and becomes one, heart, leaving your pining behind you came to the fiery Lord's side.
806.nuance: இரதம் is read as இரசம், mercury, whose scattered globules run together and become one body again, an alchemist's figure for a union that restores what was one; it can also be 'taste' (as in 773 and 792) or 'chariot', which gives no clear sense. விரகம் is the pain of separation, or, as விரகு, cunning. அணல் is Siva as the fiery one; அணல்பால் may instead be 'the near side'. The simile's point, that the parted rejoins its own kind, holds on each reading.

807.reading: As the dew that lies around is swept away by the sun, heart, so you won the holy feet of the guru of the right way.
807.nuance: சோதியான், the one of light, is the sun; சூறை கொளுமாறு, taking as a whirlwind takes or as plunder is taken, describes the dew's vanishing. What the simile compares is unstated: the guru's feet are the sun and the heart's bonds the dew, or the heart itself was taken up as the dew is. நீதி குரு, the guru of righteousness or of the right way, is the only human agent the work names, and he appears in its last line.

links.note: Tirumular's samadhi gives the unceasing honey of Siva's bliss which those who drink it do not leave, whether standing, sitting or lying; Pattinathar's heart drinks within and without the toddy of bliss that does not cloy. Both answer the doubt that bliss might sate or stop, and both make it a drink.

The Puranamalai's union does not cloy like the taste of honey (தெவிட்டாய்); the heart's toddy of bliss never cloys (உவட்டாத). Pattinathar uses the same claim with two drinks, once for the identity of I and you and once for the heart's attainment.

Tirumular sees and leaves the void of maya and the void of knowledge, ends the traces of effect and cause, and the bond ends in the void of calm; Pattinathar's heart leaves habit, fixed contemplation and the kingdom of silence and gains the place without difference. Both make the last step a leaving of the attainments themselves, including the knower's knowledge or the sage's silence.

Sivavakkiyar's place is where one stands without mind, life, Sakti, Sambhu, caste distinction or release; Pattinathar's is where even nishta and the great kingdom of silence are gone. Both define the final place by negating the religious goods, release in one and silence in the other, and neither puts anything positive in their place beyond a name.

Tirumular says turiya samadhi is reaching the guru's feet by the guru's way, beyond conscious and inert, once the rites are set aside; Pattinathar ends the heart's whole ascent, which walked in the fourth state (795), by saying the heart won the holy feet of the guru. Both identify the highest state with the guru's feet rather than with a doctrine.

source_issues: 801 to 807 are printed with a space before the refrain நெஞ்சமே, and 805 with spaces between words, unlike 776 to 800; the run seems to come from a differently prepared source.
806 line 1, இரதம், is obscure (mercury, taste or chariot) and may be a variant spelling of இரசம்.
